record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: Let N be the set of natural numbers. If A is a subset of N^2 such that the sum over all (x,y) in A of 1/(x^2 + y^2) diverges, must A contain the four vertices of an axes-parallel square?

evidence.quote: If A ⊆ N^2 with Σ 1/(x^2 + y^2) = ∞
A must contain the 4 vertices of an axes-parallel square

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$ and let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$ be a set of lattice points in the plane satisfying
$$\sum_{(x,y)\in A}\frac{1}{x^{2}+y^{2}}=\infty.$$
An axes-parallel square is a 4-element set of the form $\{(a,b),(a+d,b),(a,b+d),(a+d,b+d)\}$ for some positive integer $d$ and integers $a,b$.

Must $A$ necessarily contain the four vertices of an axes-parallel square?
artifact.status_search_result: This is a two-dimensional density/Ramsey question in the spirit of Erdős's conjecture on arithmetic progressions (where divergence of reciprocals forces long APs). Web searches for the specific lattice/square formulation reveal no published resolution; it is listed among open problems in Euclidean Ramsey theory and appears to remain unsolved.

status_evidence.title: Erdős Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Database of Erdős problems; analogous reciprocal-sum-forces-structure questions are listed as open.
status_evidence.claim: No solution to the specific lattice axes-parallel square question is recorded.

status_evidence.title: List of conjectures by Paul Erdős - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Includes the Erdős conjecture on arithmetic progressions (divergent reciprocals imply arbitrarily long APs), which remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The analogous reciprocal-divergence-implies-structure framework is itself open.
